title: Protocol to drive human monocyte-to-macrophage polarization in vitro using tumor conditioned media
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol to drive human monocyte-to-macrophage polarization in vitro using tumor conditioned media

### Overview

This protocol outlines the isolation of human CD14+ monocytes from peripheral blood, their differentiation into macrophages, and subsequent polarization using tumor-conditioned media. It includes detailed steps for preparing melanoma cell conditioned media, optimizing protein concentration, treating monocytes to induce macrophage phenotypes, and assessing polarization via morphological analysis and flow cytometry. The protocol also describes a co-culture assay to evaluate macrophage-mediated killing of CFSE-labeled melanoma target cells.

### Materials/Reagents

RPMI complete media (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin, 2 mM L-glutamine), DMEM complete media (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin), Serum-free DMEM (1% Penicillin-Streptomycin), PBS (-/- CaCl2/MgCl2), PBS (+/+ CaCl2/MgCl2), Trypsin (Gibco), Lymphoprep (STEMCELL Technologies), MACS buffer (PBS -/- CaCl2/MgCl2, 0.5% FBS, 2 mM EDTA), CD14 microbeads (Miltenyi), Trypan Blue, Hemocytometer, FACS buffer (PBS -/-, 1% BSA, 2 mM EDTA, 0.1% NaN3), Human TruStain FcX blocking solution (BioLegend), Antibody panel: HLA-DR-FITC, CD86-PE/Cyanine7, CD163-APC, CD206-PE, DAPI (5 μg/mL), MACS Comp Beads (anti-mouse Igκ and blank; Miltenyi Biotec), CFSE Cell Division Tracker Kit (BioLegend), IL-4 (20 ng/mL), IL-10 (20 ng/mL), M-CSF (50 ng/mL), IFN-γ (20 ng/mL), LPS (100 ng/mL), Formaldehyde (1%), Amicon-Ultra 3 kDa filter-pore falcons (Millipore), BCA assay kit (Pierce).

### Equipment

24-well plates, T12 wells, T6 wells, 10 cm dishes, 48-well plates, 50 mL Falcon tubes, 15 mL Falcon tubes, Eppendorf tubes, Disposable Pasteur pipettes, Swinging-bucket centrifuge, Midi-MACS separator with LS columns, 70 μm cell strainer, Flow cytometer (BD FACS CANTO II), ImageJ software, Microscope capable of 10-20× magnification, P1000 tips, Virkon-filled waste container.

### Safety & Sterility

Establish transfer agreements and obtain informed consent for human blood specimens. Follow institutional SOPs for handling and disposal of human blood samples in sterile laminar flow hoods. Ensure personnel have appropriate vaccinations if samples are not screened for pathogens. Dispose of supernatant by pouring slowly into a Virkon-filled container rather than aspiration to maintain safety. Keep primary cells on ice and minimize handling outside the incubator to preserve viability. Maintain all centrifugation steps involving cell harvesting at 4°C where specified. Use sterile techniques throughout PBMC isolation and cell culture.

## Macrophage Differentiation and Conditioned Media Preparation

### Day 0

1. Seed 1 × 10 ^6 CD14+ monocytes in 1 mL of RPMI complete (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin, 2 mM L-glutamine) in a 24-well plate and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO _2 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->

#### Branch A: Large cell number scaling

1. If a large cell number is required for downstream functional assays, scale up culture conditions as follows: i. Seed 2 × 10^6 cells in a T12 well with 2 mL of culture media. ii. Seed 4-5 × 10^6 cells in a T6 well with 4 mL of culture media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->

#### Shared continuation

> **Operational constraint:** Note: Primary cells are sensitive; reduce cell plate handling time outside of the cell incubator to maintain viability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
1. To prepare tumor conditioned media, harvest melanoma cells from the cell culture flask. Aspirate culture media, wash with PBS (−/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ) and incubate with trypsin (Gibco) for 1-2 min at 37°C, 5% CO _2 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
2. Resuspend detached cells in DMEM complete media (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin), centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes, and resuspend the pellet in fresh DMEM complete media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
3. Seed 2.5 × 10^5 melanoma cells in 2 mL of DMEM complete media per T6 well overnight. Plate replicate wells or adjust seeding density based on the final protein yield required. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->

#### Branch B: Large volume CM scaling

1. If a large volume of conditioned media is needed, scale up culture conditions by seeding 1.5 × 10^6 tumor cells in a 10 cm dish with 10 mL of culture media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->

### Day 1

1. Discard culture media from melanoma cell cultures. Wash tumor cells twice with PBS (+/+ CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ; Gibco). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->
2. Add 1 mL of serum-free DMEM (containing 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin) per T6 well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S03 -->

#### Branch B: Large volume CM scaling

1. If scaled up to a 10 cm dish, add 6 mL of serum-free DMEM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S04 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Incubate cells at 37°C, 10% CO _2 for 48 h for media conditioning. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S05 -->

### Day 3

1. Harvest the conditioned media from the cell culture wells and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes to remove dead cells and debris. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Keep the conditioned media on ice immediately after harvest to maintain intact protein composition. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->
2. Transfer the supernatant into Amicon-Ultra 3 kDa filter-pore falcons (Millipore) and centrifuge at 4,000 rpm in a swinging bucket rotor for 45 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S03 -->
3. Quantify conditioned media samples via BCA assay (Pierce) to calculate protein concentration levels as per manufacturer’s instructions ( https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/23227 ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S05 -->
4. Always titrate conditioned media with several dilutions to determine the optimal concentration for analysis from the BCA standard curve; dilutions of 1:2 to 1:5 in PBS work well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S06 -->
5. Note: Run serum-free DMEM as your blank control, applying the same dilution factor used for your samples. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S07 -->
6. Normalize protein from each condition by resuspending the desired conditioned media volumes into RPMI complete media to achieve a concentration of 70 μg/mL (2× stock). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S08 -->
7. Carefully remove 50% of the media (500 μL) from the macrophage T24-wells and add 500 μL of the 2× protein solution to achieve a final concentration of 35 μg/mL (1×). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Pipette slowly at this stage, targeting the side of the well to avoid disrupting the monocytes. This method helps reduce metabolic waste and increase viability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S10 -->
8. For treatment controls, include a negative control of monocytes alone (RPMI media only). Use IL-4 (20 ng/mL), IL-10 (20 ng/mL), and M-CSF (50 ng/mL) as positive controls for alternatively-activated macrophages. Use IFN-γ (20 ng/mL) plus LPS (100 ng/mL) as positive controls for classically-activated macrophages. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S11 -->

### Day 6

1. Acquire bright-field images of macrophages at 10-20× magnification in order to analyze cell morphological differences by ImageJ software (see [part 2 - Morphological assessment of macrophages] ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S01 -->
2. Collect macrophage supernatants from all conditions and transfer them into separate Eppendorf tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S02 -->
3. Add 1 mL pre-cooled PBS (−/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ) to each well and place plates on ice for 30 min where cells will start to round up and detach. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S03 -->

#### Branch A: Enhanced detachment

1. Optional: Supplement the PBS with 2 mM EDTA to promote cell detachment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S04 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. In the meantime, spin down cell supernatants at 300 × g for 5 min to collect any floating cells, and resuspend in 100 μL FACS buffer (PBS−/−, 1% BSA, 2 mM EDTA, 0.1% NaN _3 ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Perform all centrifugation steps at 4°C. Floating cells are likely monocytic or apoptotic. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S06 -->
2. After cells start to detach, gently scrape them off the well using the flat end of a P1000 tip, then use a new tip to pipette up and down before transferring the cells into a fresh Eppendorf tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S07 -->
3. Combine the scraped cells with the supernatant fractions, centrifuge the tubes at 300 × g for 5 minutes, and perform a second wash with 1 mL of FACS buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S08 -->
4. Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C, resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of FACS buffer containing human TruStain FcX blocking solution (1:20; BioLegend), and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature. Vortex gently. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S09 -->

#### Branch B: Control allocation

1. Note: Before proceeding, either take a small proportion from each individual condition to create a pool sample, or allocate specific conditions for unstained and DAPI single stain controls. Transfer these into a new Eppendorf tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S10 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Spin down samples at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C, and resuspend in FACS buffer containing a 4-color antibody mixture with a total staining volume of 100 μL per sample: HLA-DR-FITC (2 μL, 1:50), CD86-PE/Cyanine7 (4 μL, 1:25), CD163-APC (4 μL, 1:25), CD206-PE (4 μL, 1:25), and FACS buffer (86 μL). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S11 -->
2. Vortex samples gently and incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S12 -->
3. Wash samples twice with FACS buffer, finally resuspend in DAPI solution (5 μg/mL) for live/dead cell separation, and acquire live samples on a flow cytometer (BD FACS CANTO II). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S13 -->

#### Branch C: Fixation option

1. Optional: Cells can be fixed in 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, centrifuged, and resuspended in FACS buffer kept at 4°C if analysis is delayed to the following day. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S14 -->

#### Branch D: Compensation preparation

1. In parallel, prepare compensation beads to correct for fluorescence spill-over from fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (single stain controls): a. Add one drop each of MACS Comp Beads (anti-mouse Igκ; Miltenyi Biotec) and MACS Comp Beads (blank) to 100 μL of FACS buffer. b. For each single stained control, add the same antibody dilution used for staining; for example, add 4 μL of CD86-PE/Cyanine7 antibody to the compensation beads. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T3-S15 -->

### ½ day

1. Acquire at least one 10× image and three 20× images at different parts of the well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T4-S01 -->
2. Import the acquired images into ImageJ software. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T4-S02 -->
3. Generate automatic cell shape descriptor measurements (such as roundness, circularity, and area) by using the ‘freehand selection' tool to manually draw around the outline of cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T4-S03 -->
4. Cells can also be manually categorized into distinct subsets such as elongated/spindle or spread/fried egg morphologies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T4-S04 -->

### 3 days

1. Trypsinize and count melanoma target cells (A375M2, WM88), and label with CFSE (BioLegend) using the CFSE cell division tracker following manufacturer’s instructions ( https://www.biolegend.com/de-de/products/cfse-cell-division-tracker-kit-9396 ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge tumor cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes and resuspend at a concentration of 10-100 × 10^6 cells/mL in 5 μM CFSE working solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S02 -->
3. Incubate the cells for 20 minutes at room temperature or 37°C, protected from light. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S03 -->
4. Quench the staining by adding 5 times the original staining volume of cell culture media (RPMI) containing 10% FBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S04 -->
5. Wash both the CFSE-labeled melanoma cells and the macrophages in complete RPMI before setting up the co-culture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S05 -->
6. Add targets (10^4 melanoma cells) to effectors (10^5 macrophages) at a ratio of 1:10 (targets: effectors) in complete RPMI and incubate for 48 hours in 48-well plates in duplicates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S06 -->
7. Upon harvesting cells with trypsin, wash them with FACS buffer, resuspend in DAPI solution (5 μg/mL) for viability staining, and immediately acquire on a flow cytometer (BD FACS CANTO II). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S07 -->
8. Discriminate between two cell populations by flow cytometry analysis: a. CFSE+DAPI+ indicates dead tumor cells. b. CFSE+DAPI- indicates live tumor cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T5-S08 -->

## PBMC Isolation and CD14+ Selection

### (Day 0): 2 h approximately

1. Set up a transfer agreement between the research/academic institute and a suitable blood specimen provider, ensuring appropriate informed consent is obtained. Follow appropriate health and safety procedures, including institutional SOPs for handling and disposal of human blood samples using allocated sterile laminar flow hoods. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Ensure users have appropriate vaccinations to safely work with human biological samples, especially if samples are not screened for known human pathogens. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
2. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy donors are obtained from anonymized human buffy coats supplied by NHSBT (Tooting, London, UK). Dilute 50 mL buffy coats 1:2 with PBS (−/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ; Gibco; room temperature). a. For example, 15 mL buffy coat and 30 mL PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
3. Using a standard 50 mL Falcon tube, gently layer 30 mL of diluted buffy coat on top of 15 mL of Lymphoprep (STEMCELL Technologies; room temperature) by slowly pipetting to the side of the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Work quickly to maintain good cell viability. Layer the first few milliliters of diluted buffy coat very slowly onto the Lymphoprep layer, tilting the tube at a 45° angle, to avoid disrupting the interface. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
4. Centrifuge in a swinging-bucket centrifuge at 800 × g for 30 minutes at room temperature (15°C-23°C) with maximum acceleration and no brake. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Use a swinging bucket rotor as opposed to a fixed-angle rotor, and ensure the brake deceleration is set to 0 to avoid disruption of the density gradient separation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
5. Collect PBMCs from the white interface layer using a disposable Pasteur pipette and transfer into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing fresh PBS (−/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
6. Top up the solutions to 50 mL with PBS and centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature with normal brake. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: During washes, rather than aspirating the supernatant which can be harsh, simply pour out the supernatant slowly into a Virkon-filled container and dispose of it appropriately according to lab safety guidelines. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
7. Discard the supernatant and repeat the washing step, resuspending in 50 mL PBS (−/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 ). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
8. Determine the number of live cells using a hemocytometer with Trypan Blue. A 1:10 dilution often gives a good density for counting; mix well before putting it into the chamber (e.g., mix 10 μL PBMC solution, 20 μL Trypan Blue, and 70 μL PBS). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
9. Centrifuge the sample at 300 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature with normal brake. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
10. Resuspend PBMCs in pre-cooled MACS buffer (PBS −/− CaCl _2 /MgCl _2 , 0.5% FBS, 2 mM EDTA) at a cell density of 10 ^7 PBMCs/80 μL, mixed with 20 μL CD14 microbeads (Miltenyi). Mix cell solutions thoroughly and incubate for 15 min at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Keep MACS buffer on ice throughout the process. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->
11. Add 1 mL of MACS buffer per 10^7 PBMCs and centrifuge samples at 300 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S17 -->
12. After centrifugation, resuspend PBMCs in MACS buffer at a cell density of 10^8 cells/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S18 -->
13. Filter samples using a 70 μm cell strainer to homogenize the mixture and reduce the risk of causing a blockage within the column. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S19 -->
14. Place the LS column in the Midi-MACS separator where a magnetic field is applied. 15. Pre-soak the LS column by adding 3 mL MACS buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S20 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Take care at all steps to not introduce any air bubbles into the columns; pipette carefully and never let the buffer run dry. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S21 -->
15. Apply the cell suspension (magnetically labeled cells with CD14 microbeads) onto the LS column, where unlabeled (CD14-) cell populations pass through the column and can be collected in a 15 mL Falcon tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S22 -->

#### Branch A: Retain unlabeled fraction

1. Note: If other cell populations are required for other experiments, retain this fraction for downstream isolation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S23 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Perform washing steps by adding MACS buffer into the column (3 rounds of 3 mL washes). Only add new buffer when the reservoir is nearly empty. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S24 -->
2. Once all washing steps have been completed and the solution running through the columns appears clear, remove LS columns carefully from the Midi-MACS separator and place them in a new 15 mL Falcon tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S25 -->
3. Add 5 mL of fresh MACS buffer onto the LS column and push the plunger down firmly to elute the CD14+ cell fraction which had been retained within the column due to CD14+ positive selection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S26 -->

#### Branch B: Secondary enrichment

1. Optional: To increase the purity of CD14+ cells, the eluted fraction can be enriched over a second LS column. Repeat the magnetic separation procedure by using a new column (steps 14-19). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S27 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. CD14+ cells are counted and resuspended at 1 × 10 ^6 /mL in RPMI complete (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin, 2 mM Glutamine), plated in the desired multiwell plate, and incubated at 37°C, 5% CO _2 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S28 -->

### 2-3 h approximately

1. Take a portion of isolated CD14+ monocytes (<10^6 cells) and keep it on ice for the duration of the flow cytometry preparation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: As staining is performed on live cells, keep samples on ice for the duration unless stated otherwise, and perform the antibody staining step at 4°C. This will maintain cell viability and prevent cell-surface receptor internalisation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
2. Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
3. Wash once with FACS buffer (PBS−/−, 1% BSA, 2 mM EDTA, 0.1% NaN _3 ) and centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
4. Resuspend in 100 μL of FACS buffer with 5 μL of FcR blocking solution (BioLegend) for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->

#### Branch A: Control preparation

1. Note: Keep a small proportion back for your unstained and DAPI single stained control. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Top up with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S07 -->
2. Resuspend in a solution of anti-human CD14 PerCP/Cyanine5.5 conjugated antibody in FACS buffer (1/20 dilution), for staining in a total volume of 100 μL. Vortex gently to mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S08 -->
3. Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S09 -->
4. Wash with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C. 29. Repeat wash step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S10 -->
5. Resuspend samples in 300-500 μL of DAPI solution (5 μg/mL in FACS buffer) for live/dead cell viability separation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S11 -->

#### Branch B: Compensation preparation

1. In parallel, prepare compensation beads for compensation of fluorescence spill over from the fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies. 32. Add one drop of both ‘blank’ and ‘anti-mouse’ Igκ beads (Miltenyi) to 100 μL FACS buffer, and add the same dilution of CD14 antibody (5 μL), vortex gently. Top up to 300-500 μL FACS buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S12 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Transfer solutions to FACS tubes and acquire data on a flow cytometer (BD FACS CANTO II). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S13 -->
